idiom_name: trait Authenticator with impls behind Box<dyn Authenticator> or enum dispatch for a closed set
implementation_notes: No standard-library authentication exists, but traits express the seam directly: define trait Authenticator { fn authenticate(&self, creds: &Credentials) -> Result<Principal, AuthError>; }, implement it per mechanism, and either keep Box<dyn Authenticator> in a registry keyed by scheme (open set) or an enum with one variant per mechanism (closed set, no dynamic dispatch). Result<_, AuthError> replaces the nil-return convention and makes invalid credentials versus verifier unavailable explicit. The classic class hierarchy has no Rust analogue and is unnecessary.
pitfalls: Secret comparison must be constant-time (subtle::ConstantTimeEq); a plain == on a token or password digest is a real vulnerability.
Box<dyn Authenticator> needs Send + Sync to be shared across async tasks; omitting the supertraits makes the registry unusable in a multi-threaded runtime.
Blocking directory or database calls inside an async fn starve the runtime; use spawn_blocking or an async client.
AuthError values are logged; they must never embed the presented credential or any secret.
